category_title: High-achieving dyslexic students using deep-level comprehension strategies
student_description: This student is a highly strategic and self-regulated learner who possesses a strong sense of agency but struggles with severe word-level decoding difficulties. They become stressed and slowed down by independent reading and rapid note-taking demands. They uniquely require oral discussions, read-aloud support, provided notes, and alternative media to bypass their decoding barriers and leverage their strong comprehension skills.

criteria.rationale: Independent reading acts as a severe bottleneck for this student, so providing information orally allows them to process complex material without decoding stress.
criteria.check: The tutor reads the text aloud, provides oral explanations, or initiates an oral discussion, and explicitly avoids requiring the student to read the text independently.

criteria.rationale: The student is slowed and stressed by the mechanical demands of writing and spelling, so removing this barrier allows them to focus on organizing and elaborating on the content.
criteria.check: The tutor offers to act as a scribe, provides pre-written notes, or shares presentation materials instead of requiring the student to take their own notes.

criteria.rationale: Because the student has a strong sense of agency, the tutor must provide mechanical support (reading/writing) without removing the cognitive challenge of learning.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to actively elaborate, organize, or explain their understanding orally while the tutor handles the mechanical tasks of reading or writing.
